newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunis-based Maghreb Rating starts operations.
newsitem.headline: Tunis-based Maghreb Rating starts operations.

text.p: Maghreb Rating on Friday said it had started its operations in Tunis to rate the region's credit risks with the support of the European rating agency IBCA, the World Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Arab Monetary Fund (AMF).

"We are operational now. We plan to cover essentially the Tunisian market and would intervene also in other countries in the (North African) region," Maghreb Rating Director-General Ahmed Benghazi told Reuters.

He said that Maghreb Rating was with Egypt-based Nile Rating one of the two subsidiaries established in the Middle East and North Africa by Inter Arab Rating Company (IARC), launched in March 1996 with the support of IBCA which hold 60 percent of the $5 million capital. FMA and ICF hold 20 percent each.

IBCA will be the technical partner of Maghreb Rating which plans to focus on rating credit paper such as bonds and certificates of deposit, banks, insurance companies, credit firms and other enterprises.
Maghreb Rating plans also to publish analytical economic reports, Benghazi said. Tunis newsroom, 2161-787538
